existingFixParts.component: Timing chain

results.component: quality oem-grade axles
results.repairRoleEvidence: Use quality OEM-grade axles; cheap aftermarket axles are a known repeat-failure complaint.

existingFixParts.note: Complete remanufactured/new front axle assembly is the usual repair once the joint clicks (sold per side). OEM PN is ERA/GEN-SPECIFIC: 2009-2013 SH (incl. XT) = 28321SC003 (supersedes SC000/SC001/SC002), ~$350-410 OEM; 2014-2018 SJ = 28321SG010 (auto) / 28321SG000 (manual, built from 1/14/14), ~$350
existingFixParts.component: Front CV axle (half-shaft) assembly, complete — per side

existingFixParts.note: For a freshly torn boot caught BEFORE the joint clicks, re-boot and repack instead of replacing the axle. OEM boot kit is era-specific: 2014-2019 = 28396SG010 (MSRP ~$54.92, includes boot + clamps + grease); 2009-2013 = 28396AG011 (outer/BJ boot kit, supersedes AG010), qty 2 referenced on the shaft.
existingFixParts.component: CV joint boot kit (outer/BJ + grease) — early re-boot before joint wears

existingFixParts.note: The front axle nut is a self-locking single-use fastener that must be replaced whenever the axle is removed/reinstalled — do not reuse. Subaru 902170049 covers Forester front (and is widely cross-applied across the Subaru line). Torque to spec and stake. ~$3-9 each.
existingFixParts.component: Front axle/hub spindle nut (self-locking, single-use)

results.repairRoleEvidence: When replacing, this is a routine pad-and-rotor job — use quality pads (Akebono ceramic is the OE-style choice on many Subarus) and properly bed them in.

existingFixParts.note: Rear pad kit for the mainstream 2015-2019 Outback 2.5i/3.6R (5th gen, BN/BS) - the highest-search generation for this complaint. Akebono ACT1808 is the OE-style ceramic set the FIX calls out (Akebono is a Subaru OE pad supplier). ERA SPLITS you must respect: 2013-2014 (4th gen BR) uses 26696AG051; 2
existingFixParts.component: Rear brake pad set (ceramic, OE-style)

existingFixParts.note: OEM rear rotor for 2015-2024 Outback 2.5L (verified fits 2017-2025 catalog listings; same casting used on 2.5i through 6th gen). ERA/ENGINE SPLITS: 2015 3.6R uses 26700FG010; 2013-2014 (4th gen BR) 2.5i uses 26700AJ021-family - use the year/engine-correct number, never a cross-gen rotor. Price is pe
existingFixParts.component: Rear brake rotor (pair)

existingFixParts.note: Required consumable named in the FIX (slide pins must be cleaned and re-greased so the caliper doesn't drag and accelerate wear). Subaru OEM is K0777YA010 (Molykote AS-880N). CRITICAL: use ONLY silicone-based grease - generic petroleum brake grease swells Subaru's rubber slide-pin bushings and seize
existingFixParts.component: Caliper slide-pin grease (silicone, boot-safe)
aftermarketXref: Permatex 24125 Silicone Ceramic Extreme Brake Lube

existingFixParts.note: Secondary/as-needed part: if inspection finds a seized or corroded rear slide pin (a common driver of the one-side-worn, dragging-caliper failure mode), replace the pin/boot kit rather than re-greasing a bad pin. PN 26631AN00A is verified for 2020-2021 (6th gen BT) Legacy/Outback. EARLIER GENS DIFFE
existingFixParts.component: Rear caliper slide-pin / boot kit (if pins corroded)
